Good exploration of the issue, but it actually gives more credit than is due by taking all "wage stagnation" statistics for granted. Many cite household income as strong evidence that incomes are stagnant, when in fact those statistics are virtually meaningless because household size is not itself constant. Household size has decreased over time in most groups, which can make income look lower even when each individual is making more money.

The skew is even less defensible when applied across cultural and class lines, as certain groups tend to have larger or smaller households. This results in a statistic that would show "inequality" even if every individual in the country were making exactly the same amount of money.
